note: Window agent review of p0700-p0799, 2 Nov 2026.

region.text: Jambi, the Melayu Kingdom's land, absorbed by Srivijaya in 692: 'Annexed by Srivijaya: 692'; 'The state was absorbed by Srivijaya by 692'

events.note: 692: Srivijaya absorbs Melayu (Jambi). The compile applies the two 692 merge events (melayu-kingdom/ledger/1 and srivijaya/ledger/3) in opposite directions: the first moves 24 cells Melayu to Srivijaya, the second moves 103 cells Srivijaya to Melayu, so Melayu ends 692 holding all 181 cells of Jambi and keeps them to 1027. This gain hands the land to Srivijaya, as the page says; ledger/2 of melayu-kingdom (1028, 'Independence restored') then returns it. Dated 692, in the p0600-p0699 window, because the page dates the annexation to 692 and the error runs through 700-1027.

correction.text: as the dossier's 757 correction, plus the Longyou and Hexi land that the Tibetan Empire takes from the Tang in 764 and Cliopatria's 757 Tang shape lacks (Lanzhou and the Gansu land west of Long Mountain)

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's text says Hexi stays Tang until Tibet conquers Liang Prefecture in 764 ('In 764 the Tibetan Empire invaded the Hexi Corridor and conquered Liang Prefecture, cutting off the Anxi and Beiting protectorates from the Tang dynasty'), but the correction leaves out the Gansu land of tibetan-empire/ledger/31, so 117 cells of Lanzhou and the Longyou land fall to nobody at 757 and stay grey until 768.

minus.text: Yanqi (Karashahr), taken by the Tibetan Empire in 763: 'In 763 the Tibetan Empire conquered Yanqi'

correction.text: the dossier's 763 correction (Anxi and Beiting garrisons, without Yanqi) plus the Hexi and Longyou land the Tibetan Empire conquers in 764 and Shazhou and Guazhou, which fall in 786

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's text says Hexi is Tibetan 'from 764', but the correction leaves Hexi out, so the Tang snap of 763 hands 830 cells of the corridor and Longyou to nobody and they stay grey for five years until the Tibetan 768 snap. The page dates the conquest of Liang Prefecture and the Hexi Corridor to 764, so the land stays Tang through 763 and tibetan-empire/ledger/31 takes it in 764.

minus.text: Yanqi (Karashahr), taken by the Tibetan Empire in 763: 'In 763 the Tibetan Empire conquered Yanqi'

correction.text: the dossier's 768 correction (Anxi and Beiting garrisons, without Yanqi) plus Shazhou (Dunhuang) and Guazhou, which stay Tang until the Tibetan occupation of 786

keyframe_overrides.why: The Guiyi Circuit page dates the beginning of Tibetan rule over Dunhuang to 786 ('From the beginning of Tibetan rule over Dunhuang (786)'; 'Around the 770s or the 780s, Shazhou ... was occupied by the Tibetans'), and tibetan-empire/ledger/34 takes Shazhou and Guazhou from Tang in 786, but the correction leaves the 200 km Dunhuang disc out, so the 768 snap drops 190 cells to nobody for 768-785 and ledger/34 then moves nothing.

correction.text: the 705 shape without Morocco and without Algeria beyond the Kahina's Numidia: Musa ibn Nusayr takes Tangier and the Sus with the west in 708 (ledger/40, Altava ledger/41), and the shape of 710 brings the rest

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's own note says Morocco is drawn one to three years early. The page has Hassan's conquest end at Numidia c. 701 ('the long conquest of Byzacena, Zeugitana and Numidia was complete'), Musa appointed in 704/5 and 'In 708 after establishing a garrison at Tangier and beginning the consolidation of the west, Musa returned to Qayrawan'. The 701-704 keyframe already leaves Morocco out and ledger/40 gains it in 708, so 1,204 Moroccan cells are Umayyad in 705-707 only because the soft Cliopatria shape is applied. The same shape draws the Algerian Tell and Sahara (about 2,900 cells) from 705; p0600-p0699 keyframe_overrides/5-8 take Algeria out of the 692-698 shapes on this page, and the ledger brings Numidia (701) and Altava's Oranais (708), so Algeria is kept to those here too (seam with that window).

correction.text: the 718 shape plus the Byzantine land of 717 west of 36 E that Cliopatria's 724 Byzantine shape holds again (the Afyon block, inner Anatolia and Tekirdag), which the Arabs never held; Cilicia (Adana, Tarsus), which Cliopatria draws Umayyad from 718 on, is left to the 718 snap

keyframe_overrides.why: Cliopatria's 718 Byzantine shape drops the Afyon block and Tekirdag (about 260 cells) to the Umayyad shape for 718-723 and restores them in 724. The page has no Arab territory in inner or western Anatolia after the failed siege: 'the border between the two empires became stabilized along the mountains of eastern Anatolia', and from 720/721 the Arab expeditions 'were no longer aimed at conquest, but rather large-scale raids'. [Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: intersected with Cliopatria's 724 Byzantine shape. The plain 26-36 E box also restored 25 Cilician cells (Adana, Mersin: Cliopatria's 717 Byzantine land that the 718 and 724 shapes both give to the Umayyads) for 718-723 only, which moved their transfer from 718 to an unexplained 724 snap at a time the page has the Arab expeditions 'no longer aimed at conquest'. The entry now restores the 230 cells that Cliopatria drops in 718 and gives back in 724, as this why says.]

union.text: the 692 shape minus Morocco, Caucasian Albania and Iberia, and minus Algeria beyond the Kahina's Numidia
the Numidian coast and the Tebessa country (Bejaia, Jijel, Skikda, Annaba) that the 692 shape lacks and the 705 shape holds: Numidia, gained from the Kahina's state in 701 (ledger/37)

correction.text: 701-704: the 692 shape minus Morocco, Caucasian Albania and Iberia, and minus Algeria beyond the Kahina's Numidia, which the ledger gains in 701; with all of Numidia that the 705 shape holds

keyframe_overrides.why: Seam with p0600-p0699: its keyframe_overrides/5-8 take Algeria out of the 692, 693, 694 and 698 shapes (the page has the Arabs at Kairouan and Ifriqiya, Carthage in 698, the Kahina 'around 701', Musa's conquest of the west 'in 708'), but this keyframe is the 692 shape again, so at 701 it adds about 2,900 cells of the Algerian Tell and Sahara (Ouargla 735, Bechar 459, Ghardaia 289) and takes Altava's Oranais, which stays independent to 708 (ledger/41). Numidia stays: ledger/37 gains it in 701 ('after half a century, the long conquest of Byzacena, Zeugitana and Numidia was complete'). [Reviewer, 2 Nov 2026: Numidia (as the 705 shape holds it) added to the union. The 692 shape lacks 109 Numidian cells of the coast and the Tebessa country, so the 701 snap took them from the caliphate right after ledger/37 gained them and left them nobody's for 701-704, against this why's 'Numidia stays'; 103 of them are in the 705 shape and are now held from 701. The six coastal cells no Umayyad shape holds are left out.]

correction.text: Neustria's own land, Cliopatria's Neustria shape of 724 (553 cells): at its dissolution in 724 the land passes to the Frankish realm, which kingdom-of-the-franks_724 draws for 724-731 together with Austrasia and Burgundy

keyframe_overrides.why: The dossier's 'wrong' correction is the whole reunited Frankish realm (Franks 724 shape plus Neustria), which the compiler applies as Neustria's own shape: the 724 snap hands Neustria 1,541 cells of Austrasia, Burgundy and Thuringia, and when Neustria dissolves in 724 only its own 553 cells (the successor land of ledger/3) go to the Franks, so 1,526 cells (Metz, Cologne, Trier, Mainz, Strasbourg, Lyon, Wurzburg) fall to nobody for 724-731 and the Franks drop from 1,766 to 554 cells until the 732 snap. The page has Charles 'the de facto ruler of the Franks from 718 until his death', Theuderic IV on the throne 721-737, the Neustrians 'easily defeated in 724' and 'Having unified Francia under his banner'; the Neustria and Franks dossiers say the same, so only Neustria's own land should pass to the Franks at 724.
